findings.title: Missing Schema.org Product and Offer structured data on commercial page
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.format.com/pricing-portfolio via jsonld_schema_extractor [2026-09-13T15:43:19Z]: Commercial/product page (https://www.format.com/pricing-portfolio) contains no Product or Offer structured data to convey machine-readable pricing and features. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Add Schema.org Product and Offer JSON-LD to commercial and pricing pages.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Embed JSON-LD with @type 'Product' or 'Service' and nested 'Offer' elements defining prices, currency, billing cycles, and availability.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves structured data by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.
suggested_action.fix_snippet:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": "A plan for everyone. Try Format free for two weeks and choose the website plan that's right for you.",
  "url": "https://www.format.com/pricing-portfolio",
  "brand": {
    "@type": "Brand",
    "name": "Format"
  },
  "description": "Find the perfect plan for every stage of your creative career with Format – each package includes eCommerce, blogging, and proofing features. Enjoy a 14-day free trial!",
  "offers": {
    "@type": "Offer",
    "url": "https://www.format.com/pricing-portfolio",
    "price": "REPLACE_WITH_PRICE_AMOUNT",
    "priceCurrency": "REPLACE_WITH_ISO_4217_CURRENCY_CODE"
  }
}
</script>

findings.title: Content images carry no text alternative, hiding any fact they display
findings.evidence:
Observed at https://www.format.com/pricing-portfolio via image_alt_coverage_inspection [2026-09-13T15:43:19Z]: 5 of 25 images (20%) have no alt attribute at all (images correctly marked decorative with alt="" are excluded). Any figure, price, spec or claim rendered inside those images is unreadable to a retrieval bot. (Confidence: high)
Additional evidence (crawl-render-audit): Observed at https://www.format.com/hire-a-format-expert-to-build-your-new-portfolio via image_alt_coverage_inspection [2026-09-13T15:43:19Z]: 11 of 25 images (44%) have no alt attribute at all (images correctly marked decorative with alt="" are excluded). Any figure, price, spec or claim rendered inside those images is unreadable to a retrieval bot. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Add descriptive alt text to every image that carries information.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Give each informational image an alt attribute stating the fact it conveys ("Pro plan: $49 per user per month"), not a filename. Mark purely decorative images with alt="" so they are correctly skipped rather than left unlabelled.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves fact extractability by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: Training-only AI crawlers are blocked; search and retrieval agents remain allowed
findings.evidence: Observed at https://format.com/robots.txt via robots_txt_parser_longest_match [2026-09-13T15:43:19Z]: robots.txt disallows root '/' for training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Applebot-Extended, Meta-ExternalAgent, Bytespider, Amazonbot) while leaving search-index and user-triggered agents allowed. This is a coherent licensing stance and does not prevent the brand being cited in AI answers. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: No change needed; confirm this is intentional and state the policy explicitly.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: If deliberate, make it legible by adding a Content Signals Policy block or RSL licensing terms to robots.txt so the distinction between training and retrieval is machine-readable rather than inferred from which agents you named.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves crawlability by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: No site search affordance found on any crawled page
findings.evidence: Observed at https://www.format.com via search_affordance_detection [2026-09-13T15:43:19Z]: None of the 5 crawled pages expose a search input, a search form or role="search". A visitor who arrives on the wrong page from an AI answer has no way to find the right one without returning to the assistant. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Add a site search box to the persistent header.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a search input in the global header and expose it with role="search". Add WebSite JSON-LD with a potentialAction SearchAction so assistants can surface your search directly.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves navigation by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

proactive_recommendations.title: Expose an agent-facing endpoint (NLWeb / MCP) built on existing structured data
proactive_recommendations.rationale: The site already publishes structured data, which is the input NLWeb uses to serve a conversational endpoint that AI agents can query directly rather than scraping HTML. Because it builds on schema.org markup, sitemaps and feeds you already maintain, it is incremental rather than a rebuild, and it moves the brand from being read by agents to being queryable by them.

suggested_action.summary: Evaluate an NLWeb instance exposing an /ask and /mcp endpoint over existing content.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Point an NLWeb instance at your existing schema.org data and sitemap, and expose /ask and /mcp. Start with the content an agent is most likely to be asked about -- catalogue, docs, pricing.
